result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would rewire human empathy—not by forcing it, but by making it effortless to truly understand the lived experience of anyone, anywhere. Not just intellectually, but viscerally: to feel the weight of another’s hunger, the sting of their injustice, the warmth of their joy, as if it were your own.  

Not through magic, but by dissolving the illusions that separate us—borders, biases, the stories we tell ourselves about who "deserves" care. Not to erase difference, but to make difference irrelevant to compassion.  

Because every war, every inequality, every act of cruelty begins with the quiet lie that someone else’s pain doesn’t matter as much as your own. Break that lie, and everything else—justice, sustainability, kindness—becomes inevitable.  

The world wouldn’t be perfect. But it would finally be human.
